verdicts.summary: I could not break the detached, deduplicated status fetch or its backoff. A failure records its cooldown inside the fiber before the waiter's cache sees it. A call that hits the cooldown returns early and spawns nothing. The map entry is set before the fiber can run, so it cannot be left stale.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The fetch fails within 5s: Fiber.join fails, and the cache TTL reads the count that tapError already recorded at line 1300. 2) The waiter times out and the fiber later fails: the cache holds a success for 15s, and the next call is stopped at line 1280 by retryAt. 3) Ordering of statusFetches.set and delete: the fork uses startImmediately:false (line 1308) inside an uninterruptible block, so set (line 1310) runs before onExit's delete (line 1305), and the entry cannot be left stale. 4) A second waiter after the fiber exits: the entry is gone, so a new fetch starts.

verdicts.summary: The hazard this note names, the unbounded Fiber.await at line 2670, is finding 0. Its other parts check out: the map key matches, and the retry only runs when HEAD and the branch have not moved.
On an unborn branch, the retry's HEAD check fails as a separate error and hides the real ref-lock error from the pull.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The checkout is on an unborn branch that has branch.main.remote and merge set, for example a clone of a then-empty remote. The beforeSha read uses allowNonZeroExit, so beforeSha is '' (line 2672-2677). 2) `git pull --ff-only` fails with a ref-lock message, so isRefLockFailure is true (line 2693). 3) The currentSha read `rev-parse HEAD` at line 2708 runs without allowNonZeroExit, so it fails, and the Effect.all fails with that error. 4) The user sees a 'currentSha' rev-parse error and not the lock detail from line 2736. The lock-recovery path never runs.
verdicts.consequence: The pull error is misleading: it reports a rev-parse failure where the real problem is a ref lock.

verdicts.summary: The pull only waits for a status fetch that is already running. A status poll that starts during the pull can still lock the upstream remote-tracking ref, and then both the full pull and the upstream-only retry fail.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Pull starts: statusFetches has no entry at line 2667, so there is nothing to wait on. 2) While the pull runs (up to 30s), the 15s status TTL expires (line 1553). fetchRemoteForStatus finds no entry and forks a new fetch of the same remote (line 1288). The pull does not register itself in statusFetches, so nothing holds the poll back. 3) Both fetches try to update refs/remotes/origin/main. The pull gets 'cannot lock ref', and the retry at line 2723 needs the same ref. The status fetch can now live up to 5 min (line 1291), where it used to be cut off at 5s, so the retry can fail too. 4) The user sees 'could not update a local reference' on a plain pull. The race existed before this commit, but the change does not close it and the longer fetch lifetime makes it wider.
verdicts.consequence: A pull occasionally fails with a lock error caused by the app's own background fetch.
